text:
maya (sales): quick heads-up — customer asking for logs + traces to be exported to their Splunk HEC during the POC. also they want the per-request trace id echoed in responses so their ops can correlate. they ran a streaming test and hit a bunch of 429s. can we swarm? :eyes:

tom (backend): I can jump in. can you paste a sample request/headers and one of the 429 error snippets? also which route/model are they hitting (hosted vs dedicated)?

maya (sales): hosted for now. sample curl from them:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-xxxx" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -H "X-Customer-Trace: 7f3a2b" 
  -d '{"model":"gpt-neo-2-8b","prompt":"hello","stream":true}'
```
log snippet they pasted:
```
2026-01-18T14:03:22Z ERROR request_id=7f3a2b route=/v1/generate status=429 msg="rate limit exceeded" x-rate-limit-remaining=0 backend=runtime-37
2026-01-18T14:03:22Z DEBUG request_id=7f3a2b stream_chunk_timeout_ms=4500 kv_cache_size=65MB
```

alex (solutions): two quick things — (1) 429s suggest they pushed concurrency above the route's burst window; we should check the route QPS + token rate in Console -> Routes. (2) Echoing trace id: we can return X-Redwood-Trace in response headers using a simple route-level passthrough config. want me to create the exact config?

jess (infra): Splunk export: they want HEC token + TLS — easiest is to enable the log-drain on the tenant and set the forwarder to HEC. if they need traces too, we can enable OTLP export to their collector. but note: hosted RT only exports traces at 1x sampling by default for POC; if they want 100% traces we need to flip the sampling per-tenant (small perf hit).

maya (sales): they also asked about keys — do we need their HEC token or do they expect us to send to an internal collector IP? they mentioned a private endpoint behind a firewall.

tom (backend): if it's private endpoint we need IP allowlist + TLS with client certs. for immediate unblock: ask them for a temporary public HEC with token so we can validate pipeline, then later switch to private. regarding echoing trace id, try this header middleware (we can supply to hosted routing config):
```
response_headers:
  - name: "X-Redwood-Trace"
    value: "${request.headers['X-Customer-Trace'] ?: request.id }"
```
That will echo X-Customer-Trace when present, otherwise fall back to internal request id.

maya (sales): copying their ops reply — "we can spin up an HEC with token for 24h; IP is 35.194.12.7. also sending our sample trace ids."

deploy-bot: deployment started for route=customer-poc at 14:12 UTC — rollout id r-98ad. status=ok

jess (infra): notes on rate limits — for streaming endpoints we cap concurrent streams per-route. quick mitigation: reduce stream concurrency in client (recommend 4) and enable KV prefix caching for repeated prompts to reduce tokens. also we can configure a temporary higher burst_limit for this tenant in Console -> Quotas if sales approves.

alex (solutions): Splunk HEC example config we usually share with customers:
```
# Redwood -> Splunk HEC via log-drain
ENDPOINT=https://splunk-hec.company.com:8088/services/collector/event/1.0
HEADERS=(Authorization: Bearer <HEC_TOKEN>, Content-Type: application/json)
# set in Console > Exports > HTTP Forwarder
```
Also for traces (OTLP): point the tracer to their collector and set resource attributes: service=redwood-poc customer_id=acme.

tom (backend): i tried repro locally with a load script. I'm seeing the same 429 pattern when concurrent streams >6. stack trace from runtime shows backpressure: "RejectStreamError: stream queue overflow". short term we can: drop concurrency to 3-4, enable per-tenant burst (jess can flip), or add a fallback policy to non-streaming route to offload token pressure.

maya (sales): customer asked for an itemized risk checklist for Security to sign off — they want to know where logs live, retention, who has access, and whether PII is redacted. can someone draft a quick bulleted answer?

jess (infra): quick draft for them — "Logs and traces for POC are stored in tenant-scoped retention (30 days by default). Access restricted to platform SRE and Customer Ops via RBAC; exports to customer-managed endpoints (HEC/OTLP) transmit over TLS and use tokens/mtls. PII: we recommend applying client-side redaction masks; we also offer server-side scrub rules on ingest, we can enable redact patterns for the POC. Audit logs (who pulled data) will be included. For long-term we can options: private deployment or dedicated pool to meet compliance."

alex (solutions): i'll follow up with a short how-to doc for the customer: 1) create HEC token and whitelist Redwood IP, 2) send us HEC endpoint+token, 3) we'll enable log-drain for 24h and test, 4) echo header config applied, 5) run load tests with reduced concurrency and monitor Console -> Metrics.

maya (sales): perfect. can we schedule a 30m call at 2pm PST to walk ops through enabling the HEC and watch live logs in Splunk?

tom (backend): I'll be on the call and will have a debug build ready to toggle higher burst limits if they still see 429s.

jess (infra): I'll prep an OTLP endpoint we can point to if they prefer traces instead of Splunk ingestion.

maya (sales): awesome — thanks all. I'll send calendar invite and ask customer to create a temporary HEC token. :thumbsup:
